source_document.body:
Anduril Industries plans to invest $3.7 billion in a new Maryland shipyard that will manufacture parts for the Navy’s Virginia-class submarines and create 3,100 jobs . The company announced the project Tuesday at Tradepoint Atlantic in Sparrows Point, Baltimore County.
What’s Related
The facility, called Arsenal-2, will cover about 2 million square feet, with initial operations expected in 2030. Permitting will begin immediately, but construction depends on securing the necessary approvals.
The Navy separately awarded Anduril a contract worth up to $2.9 billion, with payments tied to production results. That contract is separate from the company’s planned $3.7 billion private investment.
Anduril plans to start with components such as torpedo tubes before expanding into larger submarine modules and hull sections. General Dynamics Electric Boat and HII’s Newport News Shipbuilding will assemble the submarines, with Anduril supplying parts for their production lines.
RELATED: Anduril to Build Giant Drone Factory in Ohio With $310M Grant
Speeding up delays
The project is designed to help address delays in submarine construction by adding another source of critical parts. A senior administration official told reporters that torpedo tubes are among the components holding up Virginia-class submarines already under construction, according to WMAR-2 News .
The Maryland site will occupy 187 acres and include fabrication and assembly areas, production lines, and a 1,200-foot graving dock, a dry dock used for ship work. Production is expected to increase over time after the facility starts operating.
Anduril’s plan comes as the Navy struggles to reach its goal of two Virginia-class submarines annually. Breaking Defense reported that a July Government Accountability Office report identified late supplier deliveries and a shortage of experienced workers as problems slowing the program.
“We need to grow the maritime industrial base, the submarine industrial base, so that we can produce more submarines,” Chris Brose, Anduril’s president and chief strategy officer, told reporters, according to Breaking Defense.
California facility will prepare for Maryland
Anduril also plans to manufacture submarine parts at a new, 160,000-square-foot facility in Orange County, California. That location will give the company a two-year head start on developing manufacturing methods, production workflows, and quality systems before Arsenal-2 begins operating, according to Breaking Defense.
The California operation will make test assets and maritime components, including torpedo tubes, while recruiting and training an early workforce. Anduril says the location will continue other maritime manufacturing work after the Maryland shipyard opens.
For Arsenal-2, the company plans to recruit Baltimore-area workers, including recent high school graduates, vocational program graduates, and people with aerospace or automotive manufacturing experience. Anduril says its training approach is designed to bring in workers without years of shipbuilding experience, WMAR reported.
Incentives need approvals
Maryland and Baltimore County have committed to match up to 13% of Anduril’s anticipated private investment through existing incentives and proposed new funding. New appropriations would require approval from the Maryland General Assembly and Baltimore County Council, according to WMAR.
The county’s proposed contribution includes a personal property tax break worth up to $210 million over 30 years, WYPR reported. Legislation was introduced Monday, with public sessions scheduled for October 13 and 27 before an expected vote in early November.
Arsenal-2 would bring large-scale ship manufacturing back to the former Bethlehem Steel shipyard area. Tradepoint Atlantic purchased the abandoned industrial property in 2014 and has since redeveloped it for logistics businesses , according to WYPR.
